title: Density of a specified set of rational points survives field extension
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-pc-scheme], and let $D\subseteq X(k)$ be a set of $k$-rational points [def-pc-rational-point] whose images are Zariski dense in $X$, meaning that every nonempty open subset of $|X|$ contains the image of some $d\in D$. For every field extension $L/k$ [def-pc-field-extension], put $X_L=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}L$ [def-pc-base-change, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The images of the induced points $d_L:\operatorname{Spec}L\to X_L$, for $d\in D$, are Zariski dense in $X_L$. There is no finite type, reducedness, irreducibility, separatedness or separability hypothesis. The empty scheme and the empty family are allowed.

source.place: Corollaire (11.10.7), printed p.172, applied to the family Spec(k) → X; its reduced-closure conclusion gives the assertion also for nonreduced X. Compare BLR 5.3 proof of Lemma 6, printed pp.125–126 (PDF pp.131–132).

proof.text: Fix an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, and let $E=\{d\in D:d(\operatorname{Spec}k)\in U\}$. This family is dense in $U$: a nonempty open in $U$ is also a nonempty open in $X$. Each $d\in E$ factors through $U$, and the affine spectrum correspondence gives a $k$-algebra map $u_d:A\to k$. The inverse image $U_L\subseteq X_L$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso], with coordinate ring $B=L\otimes_k A$. Equivalently use $B=A\otimes_k L$, via the isomorphism $\lambda\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes\lambda$, whose inverse reverses the factors. On this chart $d_L$ corresponds to $u_{d,L}:B\to L$, $a\otimes\lambda\mapsto u_d(a)\lambda$: the tensor algebra universal property gives this map and its two restrictions are exactly the two maps defining the induced point. Its underlying point is the prime $\ker u_{d,L}$; likewise the point $d$ of $U$ is $\ker u_d$.

source.place: Tags 01I4 (lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes) and 01JR (lemma-open-fibre-product); affine evaluation description of the family in EGA IV_3 11.10.7.

proof.text: Put $K=\{a\in A:u_d(a)=0\text{ for every }d\in E\}$. If $a\in K$, the basic open $D(a)$ contains none of the points of $E$, by [lem-weil-pbc-basic-open-function]. It is open, so density of $E$ makes it empty. Consequently $a$ is in every prime ideal of $A$, and [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq], with $I=(0)$, implies $a^n=0$ for some $n\ge1$. Conversely a nilpotent has zero image under every $u_d$, because a field has no nonzero nilpotents. Thus $K$ consists precisely of the nilpotent elements of $A$; in particular this argument does not assume $U$ reduced.

source.place: Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), radical as intersection of primes; openness and evaluation from schemes.tex Tag 01HZ (lemma-f-open).

proof.text: Regard the maps $u_d$ as $k$-linear maps on the vector space $A$. Apply [lem-sfb-common-linear-kernel-field-extension] with $F=k$, $V=A$ and index set $E$. Its hypotheses allow arbitrary $A$, $E$ and $L/k$, including the empty family. It says that every $f\in B$ with $u_{d,L}(f)=0$ for all $d\in E$ can be written $f=\sum_{i=1}^r a_i\otimes\lambda_i$ with $a_i\in K$ and $\lambda_i\in L$. Here a term $\lambda_i(a_i\otimes1)$ is $a_i\otimes\lambda_i$.

source.place: 11.10.6–11.10.7, printed p.172; agent affine coefficient implementation using the existing common-linear-kernel lemma.

proof.text: For each $a_i$ in step 3 choose $n_i\ge1$ with $a_i^{n_i}=0$, by step 2. The multiplication formula of [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] gives $(a_i\otimes\lambda_i)^{n_i}=0$. If $r>0$, set $N=1+\sum_{i=1}^r(n_i-1)$. On expanding $f^N$ by distributivity, each summand is a product of $N$ of these $r$ commuting terms. At least one term occurs $n_i$ times, since otherwise the total number of factors is at most $N-1$. Every summand is therefore zero, and $f^N=0$. If $r=0$, then $f=0$, so exponent $1$ suffices. Thus every function vanishing at all the induced points is nilpotent; no uniform bound on the nilpotents of $A$ is needed.

source.place: 11.10.7, printed p.172; agent elementary finite-sum nilpotence calculation spelling out the nonreduced case.

proof.text: Let $C\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$ be closed and contain all the points $d_L$ with $d\in E$. By the definition of the Zariski topology write $C=V(J)$ for an ideal $J\subseteq B$. For every $f\in J$ and every $d\in E$, inclusion of $\ker u_{d,L}$ in $C$ means $f\in\ker u_{d,L}$. Steps 3–4 make $f$ nilpotent, so $f$ belongs to every prime of $B$ (if $f^N=0$ is in a prime, repeated primality gives $f$ in that prime). Hence $J$ is contained in every prime, and $C=\operatorname{Spec}B$. The induced points are dense in $U_L$. The inverse images of the affine opens $U$ cover $X_L$. Given any nonempty open $W\subseteq X_L$, choose a chart meeting $W$; density on that chart gives $d_L\in W\cap U_L$ for some $d\in E\subseteq D$. This is the required density. If $X$ is empty the conclusion is vacuous. If $D$ is empty, density forces $X$ empty by taking the open $X$ itself. All tensor sums and the affine argument also allow the zero ring.

split_report.summary: Checked EGA IV_3 11.10.7 for arbitrary schemes. Preserve statement and all hypotheses. Assemble on an affine open cover. No new nodes, no Lean writing or compilation.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q106-662f7d38e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item only, with no new nodes. The statement is unchanged and is true. It is EGA IV_3 (11.10.7), printed p.172, applied to the family Spec k -> X: with Y_red = X_red the conclusion is Y' = Y⊗k', so |Y'| = |X_L|. EGA makes no finiteness assumption. I tested small cases: k[ε]/(ε²) with one point (the evaluation kernel is (ε), not 0, and the proof keeps that kernel); A^1 over an infinite field; and D = ∅, which forces X = ∅. Steps: (1) The chart lemma, with W = Spec k, V = U = Spec A and t^{-1}(W) = Spec L, gives Spec(L⊗A) with the right projections. The ring map of d_L follows from the tensor universal property (2)+(3) and the affine spectrum node. (2) basic-open-function (a),(b) plus zero-locus with I = 0 show the common evaluation kernel is exactly the nilradical. (3) common-linear-kernel-field-extension, with F = k, V = A and the index set E, matches B and u_{d,L} exactly. Its hypotheses allow arbitrary V, E and L/k. (4) The nilpotence argument of the finite sum is correct with N = 1+Σ(n_i−1), and it is genuinely elementary. (5) V(J) closed and containing the points makes J nilpotent, so C = Spec B. The affine cover then gives density on X_L. No qc or separatedness is needed. Duplicate check: separable-point-closure-universal-density, dense-rational-closed-subscheme-descent, nagata reduced-dense-image-schematic and dense-flat-pullback need extra hypotheses or state other things. None is a duplicate. The tool_use lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso (unit sk-thm-p1) is accepted as a generic black-box chart lemma. The ten recorded searches cover all required kinds. No changes made.
